summary: Tenant sticky-handoff leads to transient model rebinding during preemptive autoscaler eviction
description:
Issue summary:
During a scheduled capacity contraction triggered by the dedicated autoscaler (preemptive eviction window), several tenants experienced transient rebinding of model pins mid-session. Affected requests were routed to an older model variant for a subset of in-flight streaming sessions, causing partial/duplicate tokens and degraded output coherence for ~30 minutes.

Impact:
- Customer: BrightHealth AI (dedicated pool) reported increased token hallucinations and truncated streaming responses in prod us-east.
- Scope: ~120 streaming sessions across 3 application endpoints, estimated 0.5% of total tenant requests in the window.
- User-visible: incomplete structured JSON outputs, repeated token prefixes and occasional 502 from the edge when the session reconnect attempted to resume.

Environment:
- Dedicated GPU pool: dpool-us-east-3 (mixed reserved + spot).
- Autoscaler policy: preemptive_scale_down enabled; spot eviction threshold 15m.
- Rollout config: canary weight=10%, staged drain=false for ongoing promote. Some tenants had explicit model pins applied via the API.

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1. Tenant pins model redwood-open-13b-v1 via tenant config.
2. Start multiple long-lived streaming sessions that keep KV cache hot (chat-like usage).
3. Trigger autoscaler preemptive eviction simulation in staging (scale down spot nodes).
4. Observe some streams switch mid-session to redwood-quant-13b-v1 (legacy variant) for a few tokens before failing back.

Observed logs / metrics (snippets):
- edge-proxy: "session=abc123 lease=stale handoff=initiated target_variant=redwood-quant-13b-v1"
- orchestrator: "pin-handoff request queued for tenant=brighthealth; source_node=pool-node-17; dest_node=pool-node-4; status=partial_commit"
- serving-runtime: "kvcache-miss session=abc123 migration_in_progress=true tokens_streamed=6"
- dashboard spike: per-token latency spike from 40ms -> 220ms and increase in model mismatch error tags.

Initial hypothesis:
- Preemptive eviction caused asynchronous pin handoff: orchestrator sent a rebind to route the tenant, but the edge session lease renewal and KV cache migration did not complete atomically. As a result, in-flight streams saw the routing layer accept the connection to the fallback variant while the destination node had a cold KV cache, producing partial/duplicated tokens.
- Staged drain=false (ongoing cutover) made the window shorter and increased race probability.

Investigation notes:
- Correlated autoscaler eviction timestamps (2026-03-10T02:15Z) with session anomalies.
- Retrieved orchestrator traces showing several "partial_commit" states where the handoff state machine did not progress to "committed" before the edge replayed the session on the destination.
- Found edge-proxy code path did not check the handoff commit flag when resuming streaming sessions — it relied on a lease token that was refreshed but not tied to the pin commit.
- Confirmed that the fallback variant (quantized model) was compatible but had different tokenization boundaries; combined with KV cache cold-start it produced duplicated prefixes.

Immediate mitigations applied (2026-03-10 02:30Z):
- Support set the autoscaler preemptive eviction window to conservative mode for BrightHealth's pool (bypass preemptive for 1 hour).
- Enabled staged drain=true for rolling deploys for customer pool to force synchronous draining of sessions.
- Applied an edge-proxy temporary guard: reject session resumes for a tenant until orchestrator commit_flag==true (hotfix).

Root cause and long-term fix:
- Root cause: race between orchestrator pin-commit state and edge session resume path during preemptive node eviction; design assumption that lease refresh implied commit was false.
- Fix implemented: orchestrator PR-1128 introduces an explicit pin-commit handshake; edge-proxy updated in PR-879 to validate commit token before resuming streaming connections. Patch ensures KV cache warmup is requested and confirmed as part of the commit handshake.
- Rollout plan: staged rollout to us-east with canary weight=0 -> 25% -> 100% behind a feature flag; add observability metrics for "handoff_commit_latency" and a dashboard alarm.

Resolution notes:
- Hotfix and guard prevented further occurrences; full patch released to prod us-east on 2026-03-11 04:00Z.
- BrightHealth AI confirmed behavior returned to normal and provided sample session transcripts that are now consistent.
- Follow-up: postmortem written and scheduled runbook update to require drain=true for any autoscaler preemptive policy by default for dedicated pools with active pins.

References and crosslinks:
- Slack: #support (thread tX1f2lK) 
- Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/serving/handoff-views
- PRs: github.com/redwood-inference/orga/PR-1128, github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/PR-879
